newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to launch major customs enquiry - source.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to launch major customs enquiry - source.

text.p: Argentina's President Carlos Menem will announce later Tuesday that he is appointing a special administrator to run and investigate the nation's corruption-ridden customs service, a government source said.
Menem will make the announcement in an address to the nation on television, the official told Reuters.
The government believes that corrupt customs officials have set up a "parallel customs service" to smuggle in goods worth around $10 billion -- costing the state $3 billion in lost duties.

In a series of raids in recent days, police seized goods and documents from major retail chains including French-owned supermarkets Carrefour and U.S.-owned Wal-Mart. They have also raided customs offices, banks and warehouses.
Supermarket officials denied they had knowingly bought smuggled goods.
Seven people have been arrested, including one customs official and six customs "fixers", and 10 others are on the run from the police.
